challengeTypes: identify: What are the TWO main components of the environment? (Biotic (living) and Abiotic (non-living) vs Plants and Animals only | Air and Water only | Land and Sky only)
sort: Drag each component to biotic or abiotic (Plants = Biotic | Animals = Biotic | Air = Abiotic | Water = Abiotic | Soil = Abiotic | Sunlight = Abiotic | Humans = Biotic | Microbes = Biotic)
identify: Which of these is a NATURAL disaster? (Earthquake vs Festival vs Election | Holiday)

sort: Drag each natural disaster to its correct description (Earthquake = shaking of the earth's surface | Flood = overflow of water on normally dry land | Drought = long period without rain | Cyclone = strong rotating wind storm | Volcanic eruption = molten lava from a volcano | Tsunami = large ocean wave from underwater earthquake)
identify: Which of these is a RENEWABLE natural resource? (Water vs Coal vs Petroleum vs Natural gas)

sort: Drag each resource to renewable or non-renewable (Water = Renewable | Solar energy = Renewable | Wind energy = Renewable | Coal = Non-renewable | Petroleum = Non-renewable | Forests = Renewable if managed | Minerals = Non-renewable | Soil = Renewable if conserved)

identify: What is CONSERVATION of natural resources? (Using resources wisely and protecting them for the future vs Using up all resources quickly | Ignoring resources | Selling resources to other countries)

sort: Drag each conservation method to the resource it protects (Plant more trees = Forests | Reduce, reuse, recycle = All resources | Rainwater harvesting = Water | Use public transport = Petroleum | Avoid overgrazing = Soil | Use solar panels = Reduce coal use | Treat sewage before disposal = Water | Do not waste food = All resources)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Environment components — Environment is everything around us. Two main components: Biotic (living) — plants, animals, humans, microbes. Abiotic (non-living) — air, water, soil, sunlight, temperature. Both interact to form ecosystems. (2) Natural disasters — Events caused by nature that cause damage. Earthquake: shaking of earth's surface due to tectonic plates. Flood: overflow of water on dry land due to heavy rain. Drought: long period without rain, causing water shortage. Cyclone: strong rotating wind storm. Volcanic eruption: molten lava from a volcano. Tsunami: large ocean waves caused by underwater earthquakes. Effects: loss of life, property damage, food shortage, disease. (3) Natural resources — Materials from nature that humans use. Renewable: can be replenished — water, solar energy, wind energy, forests (if managed). Non-renewable: cannot be replenished — coal, petroleum, natural gas, minerals. Conservation: using resources wisely, reducing waste, reusing and recycling, protecting for future generations. Methods: plant trees, rainwater harvesting, reduce-reuse-recycle, use public transport, use solar/wind energy, treat sewage, avoid overgrazing. Misconceptions: 'the environment is only about trees' (WRONG — the environment includes both living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) components: air, water, soil, sunlight, plants, animals, humans), 'natural disasters are caused by humans' (WRONG — natural disasters like earthquakes, floods, and cyclones are caused by natural processes, though human activities can worsen their effects), 'coal and petroleum are renewable' (WRONG — coal and petroleum take millions of years to form and are non-renewable; they will run out), 'conservation means not using resources at all' (WRONG — conservation means using resources WISELY and not wasting them, not stopping use completely), 'forests are non-renewable' (PARTIALLY WRONG — forests are renewable IF managed properly through replanting; they become non-renewable if cut down faster than they regrow).
